options.title: Trim Airlines, Add Energy as Natural Hedge
options.best_for: Investors wanting active risk management without full defensive rotation
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
| Asset | Allocation | Change |
|---|---|---|
| DAL | 10% | -15% (trim) |
| UAL | 5% | -10% (trim) |
| Energy ETF (XLE, 0.10% ER) | 15% | new |
| QQQ | 40% | unchanged |
| VWIGX | 20% | unchanged |
| Cash | 10% | +10% |

### Why this works
Energy stocks (XLE) have inverse correlation to airlines in oil shocks — your losses on DAL/UAL are partially offset by XLE gains.

### Pros
- Natural hedge reduces net exposure to oil
- Cuts airline concentration from 40% to 15%

### Cons
- Transaction costs + STCG tax on DAL/UAL sale
- Oil shock may be transient — potential buy-high timing risk

### Agent guidance
Consider this if the Hormuz situation looks like it will persist 3+ months. Note: DAL's 10-Q discloses ~50% near-term fuel hedging, so their actual earnings impact is roughly half of the headline number.

options.title: Defensive Rotation — Domestic Staples and Gold
options.best_for: Risk-averse investors wanting to minimise further drawdown
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
| Asset | Allocation | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Consumer Staples ETF (XLP, 0.10% ER) | 25% | new |
| Short-term US Bonds (SHY, 0.15% ER) | 20% | new |
| Gold ETF (GLD, 0.40% ER) | 15% | new |
| Cash | 15% | new |
| QQQ | 25% | -15% |
| Airlines | 0% | exit all |

### Why this works
Geopolitical oil shocks historically benefit gold (+5-12%) and favour domestic consumer staples. Exiting airlines removes the direct oil-cost risk.

### Pros
- Significantly reduces drawdown risk
- Gold historically outperforms in oil-spike scenarios

### Cons
- Full airline exit triggers significant STCG tax
- VWIGX exit incurs FX conversion fee 0.5-1.5%

### Agent guidance
Only choose this if you have a specific near-term cash need or very low tolerance for further volatility.

options.title: Hold and Monitor — Geopolitical Risk Is Historically Transient
options.best_for: Long-term investors who believe supply disruptions resolve within 3-6 months
options.content_md:
### Asset Allocation
No changes. Set monitoring thresholds.

### Why this works
Historical precedent: 2018 oil shock (similar cause) resolved in 8 weeks. DAL recovered within 6 months. If you sell at the bottom, you risk missing the entire recovery.

### Pros
- No transaction costs
- No tax crystallisation
- Avoids buy-high-sell-low trap

### Cons
- Portfolio could fall further if situation escalates
- 2022 sustained inflation: QQQ -40%, airlines -38%

### Agent guidance
Set a mental stop-loss (e.g., -35% from today) and only act if breached. Avoid permanent decisions based on temporary headlines.
